title: From real plant to responsive simulation
scope: One reference-informed specimen. Scripted probe tests in MuJoCo; no learned harvesting policy or real-plant validation.
objective: Trace the evidence behind the plant: what Astra observed, what changed in the model, and how each physical interaction was checked.

sources.title: The compressed stem at the plant base
sources.observation: The crown connects leaf bases and roots in a compact, irregular structure. It is not a smooth exposed bulb.
sources.application: Replaced the large ellipsoid with a smaller irregular crown at the substrate line. Added overlapping basal sheaths and distributed stalk origins.
sources.boundary: This exposed bare-root specimen clarifies anatomy; it does not establish the visible shape or dimensions of our growing plant. Root mechanics are omitted.
sources.credit: Photograph: Gerald Holmes, Cal Poly Strawberry Center. Local study copy; redistribution rights not assumed.

sources.title: Leaflets, serrations and short connecting stalks
sources.observation: A strawberry leaf has three broad, serrated leaflets with short petiolules. Their outline and central crease matter at tool scale.
sources.application: The mesh generator consumes a manually estimated width profile from the reference. Bending leaflets use the same wedge surfaces for visual and collision geometry.
sources.boundary: The outline is reference-informed, not a calibrated 3D scan. Four hinges per leaflet approximate bending; vein details are visual only.

sources.title: Peduncle and branching pedicels
sources.observation: Fruit attach to branching stalks; they do not each originate independently at a central hub.
sources.application: Constructed a branching peduncle/pedicel graph. Fruit attach at branch ends, and gravity plus trough contact determine the settled pose.
sources.boundary: Hidden connections and depth remain inferred. Stiffness and damping have not been measured on a real stalk.

sources.title: Tabletop strawberry crop structure
sources.observation: The crop has uneven foliage, mixed fruit maturity and hanging trusses supported by the trough edge.
sources.application: Recorded visible image landmarks, separated uncertain connections, and built one representative specimen before generating a whole crop.
sources.boundary: A row photograph cannot prove that every visible stalk belongs to one crown. Camera and depth are approximate; this is not exact reconstruction.
sources.credit: Ohio State Kubota Lab page; tabletop photograph credited in-image to Meteor Systems.

sources.title: Crown anatomy in section
sources.publisher: UC IPM / Cal Poly Strawberry Center
sources.observation: Internal crown anatomy belongs to a compressed stem with leaf-base attachments, rather than a swollen root bulb.
sources.application: Used the section to constrain the external crown interpretation. Kept the crown compact and partially at the substrate surface.
sources.boundary: This is anatomical reference. Internal vascular tissues are not simulated.
sources.credit: Strand 2008 / UC IPM, reproduced by Cal Poly with permission. No redistribution license inferred.

sources.title: Variation at the fruit attachment
sources.observation: Calyx shape and size vary around the fruit attachment. A single repeated star-shaped cap does not capture that variation.
sources.application: Retained the source as a constraint for the next morphology pass. Current calyx detail remains a visual approximation.
sources.boundary: Calyx contact, fruit bruising and detachment are not implemented. This reference has not yet been fully transferred to geometry.

sources.title: Achenes and the fruit surface
sources.observation: Surface features are embedded in the fruit form and include achene and pistil-remnant detail.
sources.application: Recorded the evidence for future surface and maturity-specific geometry work; existing fruit remain rigid bodies.
sources.boundary: Visible seed details do not establish a contact-accurate surface or a validated bruising model.

sources.title: Open flower anatomy
sources.observation: Flowers are a separate developmental stage with petal, sepal and central reproductive structures.
sources.application: Added a reference for future maturity variation. The current contact specimen does not include simulated flowers.
sources.boundary: Source retained for planning; no flower geometry or mechanics are claimed.

revisions.title: Build the structure before multiplying plants
revisions.observation: Repeated procedural foliage and centrally arranged stalks were not convincing as one connected plant.
revisions.decision: Use a visible landmark graph and botanical topology, while recording hidden connections as assumptions.
revisions.change: Built a single crown with five trifoliate leaves and an independently branching fruit truss. Leaf meshes use the stored reference width profile.
revisions.evidence: The current specimen has inspectable connections and shared visual/collision leaf surfaces. Its depth and metric dimensions still need measurement.

revisions.title: Reject the overlapping probe initialization
revisions.observation: An early neighboring-fruit probe began inside geometry, producing an approximately 8.9 mm penetration.
revisions.decision: Reject that diagnostic rather than interpret an initialization impulse as plausible plant behavior.
revisions.change: Selected a collision-aware approach and paired it with an identical no-contact trajectory. Kept the failed checkpoint for inspection.
revisions.evidence: The current three probe trials start without contact. Matching controls produce zero probe contacts. This validates initialization and contact attribution, not biological accuracy.

revisions.title: Replace the bulb with a compact crown
revisions.observation: The plant base looked like a large smooth bulb, with disconnected-looking stalk origins.
revisions.decision: Use the bare-root and section references to model a compact compressed stem with overlapping bases at the substrate line.
revisions.change: Reduced and irregularized the crown, distributed stalk origins, and attached basal sheaths to their bending stalk bodies.
revisions.evidence: The close-up exposes the revised connections. Re-ran all three contacts and their controls on the saved v4 model. The crown is still fixed and roots are omitted.

revisions.title: Keep the contact evidence inspectable
revisions.observation: A stable simulation or attractive render alone could hide missed targets, incidental contacts or untested assumptions.
revisions.decision: Inspect each contact separately and preserve numerical results alongside close-up video and orbitable recorded geometry.
revisions.change: Recorded leaf brushing, stalk bending and cluster response from the settled plant, with matched collision-disabled controls.
revisions.evidence: All intended targets were touched, controls had zero probe contacts, and no physics warnings were recorded. Transient settling penetrations exceeded 1 mm; material calibration remains outstanding.

experiments.title: Leaf brushing
experiments.question: Does a tool touch and bend the leaf where it appears to?
experiments.method: A force-limited scripted probe crosses a selected leaflet. The paired control uses the same start state and trajectory with probe collision disabled.
experiments.finding: The intended leaf surface was touched. Its neighboring strips also registered contact, consistent with a finite-size probe.
experiments.limitation: This tests collision placement and response. Leaf stiffness, damping and failure behavior are uncalibrated.

experiments.title: Stalk bending
experiments.question: Does stalk contact transmit motion through the connected plant?
experiments.method: A force-limited scripted probe pushes the selected peduncle after ten seconds of settling. The matched no-contact control retains the same probe trajectory.
experiments.finding: The intended stalk segment was touched. The result file preserves incidental probe contacts and the response of the connected truss.
experiments.limitation: Capsule chains approximate elasticity. The observed motion is not a measured match to a living stalk.

experiments.title: Neighboring fruit
experiments.question: Does pushing one berry affect the surrounding cluster?
experiments.method: A collision-aware scripted probe approaches a selected berry. Fruit can transmit contact through the cluster and stalk network.
experiments.finding: The intended berry was touched without initial probe overlap. Neighboring fruit already touch at rest, so this is a cluster-response trial.
experiments.limitation: This does not test first-contact onset, fruit deformation, bruising or detachment. Fruit are rigid bodies.

assumptions.subject: Plant connectivity
assumptions.value: Trifoliate leaves, a compact crown, and branching fruit stalks are supported by the anatomical references.
assumptions.consequence: The specimen follows that topology; hidden connections in the crop photograph are still inferred.

assumptions.subject: Hidden depth and metric scale
assumptions.value: Image landmarks constrain visible placement. All depth coordinates and plant dimensions are reconstructed by judgment.
assumptions.consequence: We cannot claim an exact digital twin or use this geometry as measured crop clearance.

assumptions.subject: Tissue stiffness and damping
assumptions.value: Elastic stalk chains and hinged leaflets use selected stiffness/damping values, not real force–deflection measurements.
assumptions.consequence: Contact is simulated, but force and recovery predictions need physical calibration.

assumptions.subject: Crown and substrate boundary
assumptions.value: The crown is fixed at the substrate. Roots and root/substrate mechanics are omitted.
assumptions.consequence: Whole-plant pullout or crown movement cannot be learned credibly from this specimen.

assumptions.subject: Fruit and decorative details
assumptions.value: Fruit are rigid. Fine calyx and seed geometry is visual detail; bruising, cutting and detachment are not modeled.
assumptions.consequence: Passing a cluster contact probe does not validate harvesting or delicate fruit handling.

assumptions.subject: Contact checks
assumptions.value: Simulator logs record target contact, matched controls, initial overlaps, force, penetration and solver warnings.
assumptions.consequence: These are measurements inside this simulation, not measurements of a real plant.

next_steps: Fit a consistent camera and quantify projected landmark errors against the selected specimen references.
Collect real leaf and stalk force–deflection and recovery measurements before fitting tissue parameters.
Review transient settling contacts over 1 mm and check timestep/contact sensitivity.
Improve fruit maturity and calyx geometry, then validate cutting/detachment separately before harvesting training.
Expand to multiple plants only after a coherent specimen passes visual review and the task-relevant contact checks.
